# Tagged Kobo upgrade fixtures

`v4_1_43/{emitted,seeded_only}` were generated by running
`generate_v4_1_43.py` **from a clean detached v4.1.43 checkout**, commit
`bdead55920`, using that checkout's real `cps.kobo.HandleSyncRequest`, models,
seeding and fingerprint writers. They are synthetic accounts, not copied
household data. Database bytes are gzip-compressed; the main database contains
the old app tables and the harness's metadata tables, while the attached Calibre
DB contains its data table. The runtime test restores these bytes and runs the
complete current `ub.migrate_Database` before using the current sync handler.
The generator must run against the old checkout, not the candidate.

The generator pins the fixture book's publication date to
`2020-02-03T04:05:06` before the old handler emits its page. The harness
default is Calibre's undefined year 101, which `strftime('%Y')` renders as
`0101` on macOS but as `101` on Linux under CPython 3.13 (3.14 pads it), and
v4.1.43's fingerprint hashes the whole payload, date included. A fixture
frozen on one platform would store a fingerprint the other never computes.
The generator also asserts that `cps` is imported from the tagged checkout,
not from an editable install on `sys.path`.

- **emitted:** two paired readers, one retired. The old seed sees no flat
  history and stamps both readers empty. The first reader receives a real
  `NewEntitlement`; its follow-up is silent. Its ledger timestamp is after its
  seed timestamp. The second has no emitted page and no ledger. `state.json`
  contains the actual old outgoing token.
- **seeded_only:** the old user-wide flat marker exists before first sync.
  The tagged seed copies it to both device ledgers; neither device receives a
  book entitlement. It also copies outstanding deletion 111 without delivering
  it. A later real handler call emits deletion 222 only to the first device.
  The first reader's 222 timestamp is after its seed; its copied live book and
  deletion 111 timestamps are before the seed. The second has only guesses.

This establishes the old writer's chronology rather than guessing receipt from
current book timestamps. The v4.1.43 seed called both stage helpers **before**
`mark_device_entitlement_ledgers_seeded`; actual per-device page emissions
subsequently updated the same rows. That version did not have modern pending
page acknowledgments or `change_basis`. A non-null `change_basis` on such a
row is separate, modern provenance; the upgrade audit stamps one only on a
row it has already decided to keep.

The old record cannot tell whether a particular physical reader holds a
book: another reader could have produced the same flat history, and the old
writer recorded a row when it sent a book, not when the reader stored it. The
migration keeps a row only when the account has a record of taking delivery
of its book: a `Downloads` row, reading statistics a Kobo reported, or a
reading position this reader reported. It clears the rest, so a book nothing
downloaded is announced New again instead of being starved. A book another
reader of the account, or a browser, downloaded keeps its row on a reader
that lacks it; that gap is documented in the tests and recovered by resend or
Full Sync. The tagged tests therefore record the download the reader made
(`downloaded=`) wherever they model a held book. An installation from before
v4.1.43, with no per-device ledger at all, is seeded per reader at its own
first sync, from the flat history its own sync token vouches for
(`test_pre_ledger_*` in `test_1925_kobo_sync_dedownload.py`).
